# Alerd Berd

> Alerd Berd monitors web services and sends email and Web Push alerts when they
> fail. Services expose a small, versioned JSON health contract that Alerd polls
> to derive a green, amber or red status.

Only `status` is required. Components and threshold-based metrics are optional.
The minimal response is `{"status":"ok"}`. These instructions are for operators
and coding agents implementing a health route.

## Access

This file is public; the guides require a personal API key, session or instance
spec token. Obtain a token from your Alerd operator and send it as a bearer:

```sh
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_TOKEN>" https://alerd.example.com/spec/alerd-health.schema.json
```

Without valid authentication, guide URLs return 401.

## Health contract

- [JSON Schema v1](https://alerd.example.com/spec/alerd-health.schema.json): authoritative fields, types and enums
- [Complete example](https://alerd.example.com/spec/example-health.json): components, metrics and runtime information
- [Implementation guide, English](https://alerd.example.com/spec/implementing-health.en.md): Next.js and Express examples, runtime commit reporting and the required Coolify setting
- [Implementierungs-Guide, Deutsch](https://alerd.example.com/spec/implementing-health.md): dieselbe Anleitung auf Deutsch

## Rules

- Required: `status` is `"ok"`, `"degraded"` or `"down"`.
- `components[]`: `name`, `status`, optional `detail`. A down component makes the monitor red; degraded makes it amber.
- `metrics[]`: `name`, `value`, optional `unit`, `warn`, `crit`, `direction`. Value ≥ warn is amber; value ≥ crit is red. Use `direction: "below"` where low values are bad.
- The route may require a bearer token. Alerd sends the token stored on its monitor as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- A parsed response derives its colour from status, components and metrics, rather than the HTTP status. No response, timeout or DNS failure is automatically red.
- This is an additional deep route (conventionally `/health`), separate from public, shallow liveness such as `/api/health`. Leave existing container liveness unchanged.
- Recommended: include `runtime.node` from `process.versions.node`, `runtime.commit` for the running build and exact `runtime.packages` versions from `node_modules`. This supports advisory checks and exact update confirmation. Report this information only in the protected spec route.

## Required handoff from coding agents

If the app runs on Coolify and you implement `runtime.commit`, explicitly tell the
operator to perform this manual step:

> In the app's Coolify settings, enable **Advanced → Build → Source commit
> availability → Available during build**, then redeploy. Otherwise SOURCE_COMMIT
> remains empty and the app cannot report its build commit.

After deployment, verify that the spec-health response contains the deployed
`runtime.commit`. If it is absent, check both the Coolify setting and the
Dockerfile's ARG-to-ENV forwarding.

The operator needs the full health URL and its bearer token, if protected.
Alerd configures the polling interval, fallback thresholds and alert channels.
